input:
This case sets the safety stock for the packaging film at 213 units. Mean demand is 332 units per week, the standard deviation of weekly demand is 43 units per week, and the replenishment lead time is 9 weeks. The stock is sized for a 95% cycle service level: in a cycle in which demand runs above its mean, the safety stock covers the excess up to that level, while the balance of the replenishment quantity covers mean demand over the lead time, ensuring that service is maintained in the large majority of cycles.
Demand is treated as normal and independent between weeks. Independence is the key assumption that carries the sizing: the lead-time spread is built up from the weekly spread on the basis that a high week is not followed by high weeks more often than chance gives, and a demand pattern with runs of high weeks would need a larger stock for the same service level. It is worth noting that seasonal peaks are excluded from the policy. Demand in a peak period is not drawn from the distribution the stock is sized on, and a service failure inside a peak is a failure of the exclusion, not of the stock: the peak is covered by the separate seasonal build, or it is accepted as a period the policy does not serve. Outside the peaks, the 213 units stand against the ordinary variation of weekly demand over the lead time, and the policy will be reviewed on the recorded demand, not on the assumed distribution, when the record is long enough to test it properly.
